commits.message:
feat(host): a cold host starts from the bundle the install recorded (#948)

* feat(host): a cold host starts from the bundle the install recorded

Every bar on the machine is drawn by one host, so a client that found it down must start the installed bundle, not its own. The install records its bundle in the state directory; both clients read that record at spawn time and refuse to start anything, showing why on the bar, when it is missing or unusable. The record is written only when the user's statusline command names the writing bundle, so a worktree's build or deploy never moves the host. The host's binary watch includes the record, so repointing it ends the running host, and a host no longer exits on a client with a newer protocol.

* fix(host): the install records the bundle it staged, and the dead obtainDaemon path is gone

The install records the bundle it staged when it owns the statusline
command instead of reading the command back; a checkout's deploy compares
real paths. A refused kick no longer claims to kick. obtainDaemon had no
production caller and carried a second copy of the record read.

* fix(host): a symlinked entry names the bundle it runs, and the record reads through the shared helpers

The checkout's recorder resolves the entry's real path before taking the
bundle beside it. The record reader uses the regular-file reader and the
presence stat, so an unreadable bundle is not reported as missing. The
dead state-dir guard, the vacuous mismatch-fixture flag and stale comments
go; the stale-lock reclaim test returns against the kick.

* fix(host): a customized statusline that runs the staged entry is recorded; undo a stray test reformat

A wrapper or env command that runs the staged entry is the install, so the
install records it without --force destroying the command. The previous
commit's prettier run over test/ rewrapped unrelated files; they return to
their prior text.

* test(host): a cold-start test waits for the host's answer and the node line, not the socket or the file alone

fix(tools): the dev tools run outside Jest, and nothing outside test/ imports the suite (candybar-later-fixes-nwu9.1d4)

`pnpm bar`, `pnpm bar:web` and `pnpm bench` crashed from a plain shell:
they imported the Jest suite's helpers, which read the worker's
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at import and register cleanups on the Jest file.

What a tool and a test share now lives in scripts/lib (the daemon
spawner, wire, requests, the bar driver and the draw fixtures) and
takes what the suite binds as arguments: the session environment and
the admission a daemon start passes through. The tests pass their
environment and the daemon pool; a tool passes the shell's and admits
at once, so a bar run beside the suite takes none of its slots.

The import-zone table gains test/ and the tools (scripts/, site/,
proto-looks/): src and the tools may not import test/, by the zone rule
src is already checked by, now also run over the tools with Jest's
globals refused. `pnpm bar` is tested as a child run with a shell's env.

Along the way: three TTL cases in var-sources slept one TTL and assumed
the tick had run; they now poll for the change the tick makes.
